body:
Injection attacks are often due to developers not ensuring separation between data and data structure/format.  This happens when serializing data, which is something that APIs do a lot.  I've often seen a common practice for applications to build JSON or even XML requests and responses insecurely, such as by concatenating strings or even using templated strings or format strings to build the output.

I've often recommended that secure applications will *always* use a serializer for the data format you are targeting so that those libraries can better ensure that data values are encoded properly to prevent JSON or XML injection attacks and the like.

I didn't see this in the current list.

comments.body: @jaxley - please confirm that V5.5 covers off your requirements. I think it probably does, especially V5.5.4. If that's not the case, can you please suggest a rewording for V5.5.4 that you think encapsulates your view. I personally would prefer folks using JSON over say PHP serialized objects, XML or ASN, as we know how to protect against RCE with JSON.
I'm going to close this for now. @jaxley if you disagree, it has to be today. I'm going to be working on the Word -> PDF version offline tomorrow.

I'm not quite versed in all of ASVS and had incorrectly assumed that the API specs were comprehensive.  I missed the note at the top indicating that others in the ASVS were also still applicable.

I looked at v5 and it has quite a bit of coverage.  v5.5.4 is about *deserialization* though and my concern is about how data is *serialized*.

I didn't see any of the items specifically address this concern about building structured data.  Something that would address https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/707.html

I would put something in v5.3

v5.3.6 speaks to the risk

> "Verify that the application projects against JavaScript or JSON injection attacks, including for eval attacks, remote JavaScript includes, CSP bypasses, DOM XSS, and JavaScript expression evaluation"

I think it would be best to have a general item in 5.3 since this is so prevalent across any data format.

Something like,

> Verify that building structured data outputs (such as XML, JSON, URLs, etc.), APIs are used that maintain a strong boundary between *data* and *control plane* metacharacters, including automatic context-aware output encoding are used to avoid injection attacks.
